newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coca-Cola Philippines sets $1.7 bln expansion plan.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Philippines sets $1.7 bln expansion plan.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co's Philippine unit on Thursday announced a $1.7 billion expansion programme designed to strengthen its position in the country's fast-growing soft drinks market over the next five years.

"Coca-Cola has opened its 21st bottling plant in the Philippines as part of a $1.7 billion five-year spending programme to meet growing product demand and strengthen its leadership position in the country," the company said in a statement.
Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc is 70 percent-owned by food and beverage conglomerate San Miguel Corp and 30 percent by the Coca-Cola Company.
It is the number one soft drinks company in the country, with a total market share of 75 percent.
Coca-Cola Philippines said the new bottling plant will have an initial annual production capacity of more than 31 million cases.
The new plant, located in Laguna south of Manila, is one of the largest soft drinks complexes in the world, built at a total investment of 3.1 billion pesos ($118 million), the statement said.

"The Philippines has become one of our most important markets internationally," the statement quoted Douglas Ivester, president and chief operating officer of The Coca-Cola Company, as saying during the inauguration of the new plant on Thursday.
Officials said the expansion programme in the Philippines would include plants, products and marketing.
The Philippines is estimated to have consumed about 2.2 billion litres of soft drinks in 1996.
"For 1997, we are expecting a 14 to 15 percent increase in sales volume," a company official said.
In 1996, the firm's sales increased by 14 percent. Its revenues grew 20 percent to 26.3 billion pesos and operating income rose 13 percent to 4.64 billion pesos.
Analysts said a fast growing economy and rising incomes have considerably brightened growth prospects for soft drink firms.
Coca-Cola was the first cola drink that came into the Philippines, arriving 70 years ago. Coke was then made by San Miguel Corp under a licence.
To take advantage of a fast-growing market, Coca-Cola and San Miguel set up the joint venture Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines in 1981.

"The principal growth driver for San Miguel is Coca-Cola Bottlers at 40 percent of operating income...it has managed to ride nicely on the wave of rising incomes, accelerating jobs growth and an expanding middle class since 1992," brokerage SBC Warburg said in a research paper last year.

Coca-Cola's international rival Pepsi Inc holds only a small market share in the Philippines and the competition is mainly from local soft drinks firm Cosmos Bottling Corp, which in 1996 managed to raise its market share to 15 percent from seven percent in the previous year.
